title: First Five Minutes Operator Cookbook and CSR Scripts
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
========

This page captures a compact, actionable playbook for the first five minutes of any on-call activation plus a set of short Customer Support Representative (CSR) scripts and status templates. The goal is to reduce time-to-stabilize by standardizing immediate operator actions, clarifying responsibilities, and providing repeatable customer-facing messaging. This doc is intended for first responders, bridge operators, and support agents.

When to use this playbook
-------------------------
- Pager or monitoring alert for production-facing service impacting customer requests (latency, errors, capacity).
- Customer-reported outage escalated to on-call.
- Any incident declared P1 / Sev-1 by SRE or product steward.

Key principles (quick)
----------------------
- Acknowledge fast: an initial, accurate status reduces duplicate work and calms stakeholders.
- Observe first, act second: gather evidence quickly before sweeping changes.
- Contain, then mitigate: prioritize actions that prevent damage or wide impact.
- Communicate clearly: internal and external messages should be short, factual, and time-boxed.

Operator checklist: 0–5 minutes (ordered)
---------------------------------------
1. Acknowledge and declare scope (0:00–0:30)
   - Accept the pager in the on-call system and record timestamp.
   - Post a 1-line bridge message in the designated channel: "Investigating: [service] alert — initial triage started (T+0m)."
   - Set incident priority level per SLO impact matrix.

2. Quick evidence snapshot (0:30–1:30)
   - Grab dashboards: latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99), error rate, request rate for the last 15 minutes.
   - Check recent deploys / rollouts (last 30–60 minutes): deploy pipeline, Canary status.
   - Collect top-5 logs errors (grep/ELK) and top N failing endpoints.

   Example commands:
   - kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving --selector=svc=api -o wide
   - curl -sS "https://monitoring.internal/api/v1/query?query=rate(request_errors[1m])" | jq .
   - aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs/last-hour/ . --include '*api-*' --profile oncall

3. Rapid containment (1:30–3:00)
   - If obvious noisy neighbor or hot loop, apply a short-lived rate limit until mitigation: e.g., Traffic Control: svc-level rate to 50% for 10m.
   - If a model variant or recent canary looks correlated, switch routing to last-known-good variant using the routing control plane: "route set my-service -> model:v42 --weight 100 --dry=false".
   - If persistent cache corruption suspected, toggle read-through-only mode and invalidate affected prefixes.

4. Escalate and assign roles (3:00–4:00)
   - Confirm primary bridge operator and assign a restoration owner.
   - Page +1 domain expert if not already on bridge (kernel/scheduling, runtime, infra, product steward).
   - Start an evidence capture thread: list of the artifacts being collected and where.

5. External and internal one-liners (4:00–5:00)
   - Internal: short summary in bridge + SLO impact matrix level.
   - External (CSR): use the short template (below) to let affected customers know we are investigating and will provide updates.

Decision ladder: when to rollback, route, or throttle
----------------------------------------------------
- Rollback immediately if a single recent deploy correlates with error spike and automated canary indicated failure.
- Route fallback if model variant/region shows degradation but alternative variant is healthy.
- Throttle/rate-limit when resource exhaustion or noisy-neighbor behaviors cause transient spikes.

Quick runbook authorship checklist (for the operator modifying runbook during incident)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Keep a one-line summary of what changed and why.
- Add a short "If you see X do Y" step at the top for next responders.
- List the exact commands used (no shorthand).
- Timestamp actions and add links to evidence artifacts (dashboards, logs).
- Mark the runbook change as draft and flag for post-incident review.

CSR scripts and customer-facing templates
----------------------------------------
Principles for customer messages: be human, brief, factual, and set expectations. Use the "What we know / What we are doing / When next update" format. Avoid technical jargon for general customers.

CSR initial inbound template (use within first 5 minutes):
- "Hi — thanks for reporting. We are aware of an issue affecting [feature/service]. Our engineering team is investigating; we will update you within 30 minutes or sooner with next steps. If you can share a request id, timestamp, or example payload, that helps our triage. — Redwood Support"

Public status page short message (first update):
- Title: "Partial degradation of [service] in [region]"
- Body: "We are investigating increased errors for requests to [service]. Impact: some requests may fail or be delayed. Current action: on-call team has started triage and containment. Next update: in 30 minutes."

Private customer SLA/NDA-sensitive template (for enterprise accounts):
- "Redwood Incident Reference: RWI-<YYYYMMDD>-<NN> — We are investigating an issue impacting [customer-specific surface]. Our engineering and account teams are engaged and will provide a detailed update in 30 minutes. For immediate questions please reply to this thread or contact your account manager."

Short escalation message for execs (1 line)
- "Severity [1/2] incident impacting [service]; mitigation in progress; ETA unknown. Primary owner: @name. Bridge: #ops-bridge."

Evidence collection quick list
------------------------------
- Alert trigger timeline (monitoring).
- Request traces for 10 representative failing requests.
- Sample logs (first 100 errors).
- Recent deploy hashes and canary stats.
- CPU/GPU utilization across serving fleet, KV cache statistics.

Game-day micro-drill: 5-minute focus
------------------------------------
Run this 15–20 minute exercise weekly to practice the first-five-minutes flow. Roles: pager receiver, bridge operator, CSR, domain expert.
1) Fire a synthetic alert: p99 latency spike + 5% error rate.
2) T+0: Pager receiver acknowledges, posts bridge message, collects dashboards. (3 min)
3) T+3: Bridge assigns owner, attempts containment (route fallback). (5 min)
4) T+8: CSR posts public status page and notifies enterprise account leads.
5) Debrief (5–10 min) focusing on speed of acknowledgement, quality of evidence, and message clarity.

Post-incident micro-postmortem template (to start within 24 hours)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
- Title: Incident RWI-<YYYYMMDD>-<NN> — short summary
- Impact: customer-visible symptoms, affected services, regions, % requests impacted
- Timeline: bullets with timestamps for key events (pager, containment, mitigation, full restore)
- Root cause hypothesis (initial)
- Actions taken (with command or config lines used)
- Immediate remediation and durable fixes proposed
- Owner list and ETA for each fix
- Follow-up eval: add regression test or synthetic monitor to catch the issue pre-production
- Lessons learned and blameless notes

Runbook maintenance and lifecycle for first-5m steps
---------------------------------------------------
- Every runbook referenced from this playbook must include: owner, last-runbook-test date, and a 2-line quick action summary.
- Quarterly review: runbooks with no test in 90 days are flagged and an owner is assigned 30 days to remediate.

Operational SLO thresholds referenced
------------------------------------
- API 99th latency SLO: 500ms — degradation -> Sev-2; outage -> Sev-1.
- Error rate SLO: 0.5% 5m rolling — sustained >2% -> Sev-1.
- Request drop / throttling: any unauthenticated region-wide drop >1% sustained -> Sev-1.

Appendix: Sample quick commands and snippets
------------------------------------------
- Force traffic to fallback model variant (control-plane CLI):
  redwood route update --service my-service --variant model:fallback-v1 --weight 100 --reason "Immediate containment"

- Short script to snapshot top error messages (bash):
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -euo pipefail
  timeframe="15m"
  jq -r '.events[].message' /var/log/service/errors.log | head -n 100 > /tmp/incident-errors-$(date +%s).log

- Minimal evidence JSON payload example for postmortem: 
  {
    "incident_id": "RWI-20260301-01",
    "first_alert": "2026-03-01T09:12:00Z",
    "impact": "p99 latency up to 1.8s; 6% error rate for 8m"
  }

Notes and next steps
--------------------
- After restoring service, ensure runbook authorship checklist is followed and a postmortem is drafted within 24–48 hours.
- Add this playbook to the new responder apprenticeship syllabus for onboarding.
